title: Temp Tables vs Table Variables
description: Explain when to use a #temp table, a table variable, or a CTE, and why the optimizer treats them differently.

data.text: A reporting procedure stages about 200,000 rows before joining them back to base tables. The developer used a table variable (`DECLARE @staging TABLE (...)`) for the staging step instead of a `#temp` table, and the query has become very slow with a nested loop over all 200,000 rows. Explain the trade-off and what you would change.

data.title: SQL Solution
data.code:
-- Problem: table variable estimated at 1 row, so the optimizer picks a nested loop
DECLARE @staging TABLE (CustomerID int, OrderDate date, Amount decimal(18,2));
INSERT INTO @staging
SELECT CustomerID, OrderDate, Amount
FROM Orders
WHERE OrderDate >= '2024-01-01';

-- Fix: use a #temp table so statistics exist and the estimate is realistic
CREATE TABLE #staging
(
    CustomerID int NOT NULL,
    OrderDate  date NOT NULL,
    Amount     decimal(18,2) NOT NULL,
    PRIMARY KEY (CustomerID, OrderDate)
);

INSERT INTO #staging (CustomerID, OrderDate, Amount)
SELECT CustomerID, OrderDate, Amount
FROM Orders
WHERE OrderDate >= '2024-01-01';

-- The optimizer now estimates 200k rows and chooses a hash join
SELECT c.CustomerName, SUM(s.Amount) AS Total
FROM #staging AS s
JOIN Customers AS c ON c.CustomerID = s.CustomerID
GROUP BY c.CustomerName
OPTION (RECOMPILE);   -- lets the optimizer see the actual row count at runtime

DROP TABLE #staging;  -- temp tables created inside a proc are dropped automatically, but be explicit

data.title: Explanation
data.text: A table variable is deliberately treated as having **one row** by the optimizer (no statistics, no distribution), which pushes it toward nested loop joins. A `#temp` table participates in statistics and can be re-estimated. Rules of thumb: use a CTE for a single-use expression, a table variable for a handful of rows or when you need no side effects, and a `#temp` table once the row count can exceed a few hundred or when you need indexes and statistics. `OPTION (RECOMPILE)` is valuable on the statement that reads a freshly populated temp table, because statistics are not yet available at compile time.
